html:
Hyder Ali was a soldier who rose to rule the Kingdom of Mysore in southern India from about 1761 until his death in 1782, and one of the strongest opponents of the East India Company.

He began as an officer in the Mysore army. He learned from the French how to drill infantry and use field guns, and he took over the state in the 1760s, leaving the Wodeyar kings on the throne as figureheads. He was a fast and daring general:

  • He conquered Bednur and the coast of Kanara in 1763 and Malabar in 1766, and made Cochin pay tribute.
  • He fought the Marathas and the Nizam of Hyderabad for the lands of the Deccan, and took Gooty in 1775.
  • In the First Anglo-Mysore War, 1767 to 1769, he rode to the edge of Madras and forced a peace.
  • In 1780 he invaded the Carnatic and destroyed a British army at Pollilur, starting the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

His army used iron-cased rockets, which later inspired British rockets. He died in camp in December 1782, in the middle of the war, and his son Tipu Sultan carried on the fight.
sum: Hyder Ali was a soldier who rose to rule the Kingdom of Mysore in southern India from about 1761 until his death in 1782, and one of the strongest opponents of the East India Company.
